tests.scope: Independent temporary exception-terminal probes, other copied tests filtered out

evidence: comparisonMeasurements.ts:30-34 snaps only within 2*Number.EPSILON*max(1,abs(samplePosition)); ceil/floor still define the half-open complete-sample range, and buffer-length caps remain.

For nonnegative representable integer n and normal supported rates, n/rate then multiplication incurs at most approximately one Number.EPSILON relative error; the 2*EPSILON allowance covers this. Integer indices through the AudioBuffer unsigned-long length domain are exactly representable.

Independent probe executes the actual transpiled helper, rather than a separately implemented helper: 300000 seeded round trips across 12 native rates from 8000 to 384000 and indices through 2^32-1 had zero failures.
900000 independent actual-helper cases with 0.25, 0.5 and 1e-4 frame fractions had zero accidental snapping. Existing tests additionally retain 1e-7-frame fractions at short sample positions.

Mixed-rate probe with 44109 frames at 44100 Hz and 48010 frames at 48000 Hz: shorter full file retains its final-frame impulse; longer file measures 48009 complete shared frames and excludes its last impulse. Residual continues to reject different sample rates.
New tests compare RMS values, residual frame counts and edge-impulse peaks at 44100/48000/96000 Hz; no prior assertions were removed or weakened.
results.verification_limit: Values within the declared floating-point tolerance intentionally count as the integer boundary; an absolute promise to preserve every representable fractional offset within that uncertainty neighborhood is impossible with this approach. Independent fractional probes cover values outside that tolerance, and the maximum tolerance over a 32-bit frame count is below 1.91e-6 frame.

evidence: comparisonApp.ts:2088-2121 copies measurement inputs and compares active ids, revisions and AudioBuffer identity, selection, and residual-only reference id/playback gains. Track replacement mutates a track object, but it cannot mutate the copied revision/buffer references.

RMS uses original PCM and computes new gains, so focus and prior gain changes are correctly excluded; residual depends on both and cancels them. Mute/view/layout/display/file-mark events do not alter the measured input buffers or active membership and no longer cancel.

comparisonApp.ts:2137-2141 and 2163-2180 retain in-kernel cancellation and perform a final check after the last explicit UI yield. Cancellation now throws into the status handler rather than leaving Measuring text.
comparisonApp.ts:2218-2224 suppresses status after disposal and releases busy in finally for success, cancellation and errors.
Independent run of existing targeted tests passed 72/72, including both RMS and residual at the final yield, relevant-input mutations and unrelated changes, disposal, and busy reset.

Independent temporary tests inject NaN PCM and a no-complete-sample range for both RMS/residual: 4/4 passed, status reports the error, busy clears, no result dialog is created, and gains remain unchanged.
Compared saved baseline to current tests: all existing assertions are preserved; regression-before log establishes prior unrelated-change cancellation and stuck terminal status failures.
results.verification_limit: Snapshot correctness relies on decoded AudioBuffer contents remaining immutable; inspected source loading/replacement uses buffer replacement and revision changes. Tests run the actual app measurement method and numerical kernels, while playback and host analysis are mocked.
